links.comparator_used: Original radiology report alone via usual patient portal access (no supplemental NLP-modified version)
links.outcome: Patient-reported perceived understandability (ease of understanding language, difficulty with medical terms) and objective readability scores
links.effect: Ease of understanding 4.2 ± 1.2 vs 2.6 ± 1.5 (mean-difference 95% CI 0.75-2.53, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected P = .02); difficulty with medical terms 2.0 ± 1.5 vs 3.6 ± 1.4 (95% CI -2.51 to -0.60, P < .01, Bonferroni-corrected P = .04); Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level 5.9 ± 1.1 vs 11.0 ± 1.7; Reading Ease 71.0 ± 10.3 vs 28.2 ± 12.5; SMOG 20.1 ± 12.7 vs 23.5 ± 15.7; Gunning-Fog 8.2 ± 1.1 vs 14.3 ± 1.8 (all P < .01)
links.quote: Supplemental NLP-modified radiology reports were associated with improved objective readability and higher patient-reported perceived ease of understanding in a spine surgery initial consultation setting.

design_hint: supplemental LLM-simplified reports with investigator accuracy review
